verdict: Caution: lend only to organised, domestic-demand Banarasi units with verified order books and low leverage; avoid export-dependent and unbranded handloom weavers until export orders and raw-material prices stabilise.
title: Varanasi Silk Weaving & Sarees: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Banarasi silk weaving turns imported and mill yarn into high-value sarees, and cash sits in slow-moving finished stock, not in the loom.** The weaver buys yarn and zari, weaves on handloom or powerloom, and sells to wholesalers, showrooms or exporters; value is added in design and brand, not in the weaving itself. The rating methodology flags the sector as both fixed-capital and working-capital intensive, with high funding needs [8], and working capital is driven by inventory holding plus receivables [9]. So when a proposal lands, check the inventory days and the buyer list before anything else; if finished stock exceeds a normal season's sales, ask how it will be cleared and at what discount.

## What has broken now
**Local reporting says raw material is up 20-25% and monthly export has collapsed from about Rs 1,000 crore to Rs 100-200 crore, an 80% fall.** [2] Hundreds of handlooms in Madanpura, Lohta and Bajardiha are shut and weavers are leaving the trade [2]. A separate local report says fake 'Banarasi' sarees are taking the market while lakhs of weavers lose work [3]. Peer Sai Silks reported Q1 FY27 revenue flat at INR 375 crore with same-store growth down 7.5%-7.8% on weak demand, though gross margin held at 42% [4]. Siyaram saw festive demand pick up but footfall stayed moderate and buying was occasion-driven [7]. **Read this as a demand-and-cost squeeze on the unorganised end, not a collapse of the branded domestic trade.** Note the export figures are from a September 2026 local report and the peer results are dated; treat both as directional.

## Where the growth is
**The lendable growth is in organised domestic retail and wholesale, not export order-book lending.** The UP GST pool grew 14.2% Apr-to-date against India's 6.1% [D], and India-wide textile output (IIP NIC 13) rose 13.1% YoY [D] — the state is pulling ahead of the country. The state government has said Varanasi, Mirzapur and Sant Ravidas Nagar will be developed as silk clusters [1], which is a medium-term positive for units near those clusters. Pursue showroom-led retailers and wholesalers with own designs, steady domestic buyers and a clean stock statement; avoid pure export-job workers and units whose sales depend on a single overseas buyer.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not the loom.** Because inventory and receivables drive funding [9], size the limit to verified stock and receivables, take a stock-and-receivables statement every month, and keep leverage low — rating methodology ties low leverage to financial flexibility in a downturn [10]. Take monthly GST returns, stock statements and a buyer-wise sales register; if receivables age past the stated credit period, ask for the buyer's payment proof. Prefer units with domestic order visibility over those quoting export orders that local reports say are stuck [2].

## Early-warning signs
**Watch stock build-up, buyer concentration and weaver attrition.** If finished-goods inventory rises while sales stay flat, ask for a discount-sale plan; if one buyer crosses a third of sales, ask for that buyer's payment record. If the unit's weavers are leaving — as reported in Lohta and Bajardiha [2] — capacity will fall, so ask for loom-utilisation numbers. If raw-material cost rises are not passed into saree prices, margin will compress; ask for the latest price list against the last purchase bill.
watch: Turnover falls below the prior quarter's run-rate -> ask for the sales register and re-size the limit
Inventory days rise beyond the normal season -> ask for a clearance plan and cut drawing power
Single buyer crosses a third of sales -> ask for that buyer's payment proof and set a concentration covenant
Weavers leaving or looms idle -> reassess capacity and freeze fresh capex limits
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Local reports show export collapse and 20-25% raw-material inflation shutting handlooms.
